title: Curtain — one Math Engine, rail, finials and a wave-sampled drape
description:
A parametric CURTAIN on the six-node spine — Geometry → Input Properties → Math Engine → Output Metrics → 2D Render + 3D Render.

DROP IT ON A SEGMENT and it hangs along that wall — a window's head segment is the natural host, and the rail takes the segment's direction with the drape's waves breaking into the room. Flip side turns the drape to the other face.

THE DRAPE IS SAMPLED, NOT DRAWN. A curtain in plan is a wave, and a wave is what a quad prism cannot be — so the panel is CUT into `waves × subdivision` segments and each one is a quad whose two ends sit on the sine curve: `_va = A·sin(π·i/sub)`, `_vb` the same one step on. Raise the subdivision and the polyline converges on the curve; at 4 it already reads as fabric. Every segment is extruded from hem to heading, so the 3D drape and the plan wave are the SAME geometry seen twice.

WHY THE SAMPLE STEP IS π/sub AND NOT π. At one segment per half-period every sample lands on `sin(kπ) = 0` and the wave collapses to a straight line — the curve is invisible precisely where it is being measured. The subdivision exists to put samples off the zeros.

PANELS AND SEGMENTS ARE ONE BROADCAST, not a nested loop: `kron(arange(panels), ones(nseg,1))` gives every segment its panel and `kron(ones(panels,1), arange(nseg))` its position within that panel, so the two indices multiply out into one flat table and every quad is computed at once.

DRAWING IT OPEN IS ARITHMETIC. Each panel owns a bay of `W / n`; `opening` shrinks the fabric inside that bay and `eq(_pi % 2, 0)` decides which end it bunches toward, so even panels gather left and odd panels right — a pair meeting in the middle, at any count.

FULLNESS IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. `wavePathLength` sums the actual length of every sampled segment, so the fullness ratio is the heading path over the covered width — the number a curtain is specified by — and it falls out of the same points that drew the drape.

DIMENSIONS AT THE DEFAULTS: a 1.80 m opening, 2.20 m drop, rail at 2.40 m running 2.04 m over two panels, fullness 1.51, 5.98 m² of fabric.

WHAT THIS CANNOT DO. The wave is a pure sine of constant amplitude — no gathered heading, no pleat type, no fall-off toward the hem. The drape is a vertical extrusion: it does not swing, break on the floor, or tie back.

params.name: Curtain maths
params.expr:
_natL = width
# Host frame — node, segment or space
_e1 = hcat(1, 0)
_np = rows(P)
_isSeg = _np == 2
_isSpace = _np > 2
_edges = _isSpace ? (shift(P, -1) - P) : _e1
_edgeLen = len(_edges)
_longest = max(_edgeLen)
_spaceDir = _isSpace ? row(compress(_edges, eq(_edgeLen, _longest)), 0) : _e1
_segDir = _isSeg ? (row(P, 1) - row(P, 0)) : _e1
_dir = _isSpace ? _spaceDir : (_isSeg ? _segDir : _e1)
_dirLen = len(_dir)
_axisB = _dirLen > 0 ? normalize(_dir) : _e1
_rot = rotation * PI / 180
_crot = cos(_rot)
_srot = sin(_rot)
_bx = sub(_axisB, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_by = sub(_axisB, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_axisU = hcat(_bx * _crot - _by * _srot, _bx * _srot + _by * _crot)
_axisV = (flipSide > 0 ? -1 : 1) * perp(_axisU)
_ux = sub(_axisU, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_uy = sub(_axisU, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_vx = sub(_axisV, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_vy = sub(_axisV, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_Qu = col(P, 0) * _ux + col(P, 1) * _uy
_Qv = col(P, 0) * _vx + col(P, 1) * _vy
_hu0 = _np > 0 ? min(_Qu) : 0
_hu1 = _np > 0 ? max(_Qu) : 0
_hv0 = _np > 0 ? min(_Qv) : 0
_hv1 = _np > 0 ? max(_Qv) : 0
_hcu = (_hu0 + _hu1) / 2
_hcv = (_hv0 + _hv1) / 2
_hostL = _hu1 - _hu0
_hostW = _hv1 - _hv0
# Fit to host — one uniform scale, Max never enlarges
_availL = max(0, _hostL - 2 * margin)
_notOff = fitMode != 'Off'
_exact = fitMode == 'Exact'
_sRaw = _natL > 0 ? _availL / _natL : 1
_sFit = (_notOff && _availL > 0) ? (_exact ? _sRaw : min(1, _sRaw)) : 1
scale = max(0.15, min(5, _sFit))
_s = scale
_Wd = width * _s
_Dr = drop * _s
_railZ = railHeight * _s
_amp = waveDepth * _s
_fT = fabricThk * _s
_ext = railExtend * _s
_railR = railRadius * _s
_finR = finialRadius * _s
_u0 = 0 - _Wd / 2
_u1 = _Wd / 2
_zTop = _railZ
_zBot = max(0, _railZ - _Dr)
_bodyL = _Wd + 2 * _ext
_bodyW = 2 * (_amp + _fT)
# Anchor — place the footprint by any of the nine box points
_anchorL = anchorDir == 'Top-Left' || anchorDir == 'Left-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Left'
_anchorR = anchorDir == 'Top-Right' || anchorDir == 'Right-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Right'
_anchorT = anchorDir == 'Top-Left' || anchorDir == 'Top-Center' || anchorDir == 'Top-Right'
_anchorB = anchorDir == 'Bottom-Left' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Right'
_ax = _anchorR - _anchorL
_ay = _anchorB - _anchorT
_hau = _hcu + _ax * max(0, _hostL / 2 - margin)
_hav = _hcv + _ay * max(0, _hostW / 2 - margin)
_cu = _hau - _ax * _bodyL / 2
_cv = _hav - _ay * _bodyW / 2
# Fabric — every panel and every wave segment in ONE broadcast.
# The panel index and the segment index are the two factors of a kron pair, so a 1-panel
# and a 4-panel curtain are the same four lines and the same cost.
_npn = max(1, round(panels))
_sub = max(2, round(subdiv))
_nseg = max(2, round(waves)) * _sub
_pi = kron(arange(_npn), ones(_nseg, 1))
_si = kron(ones(_npn, 1), arange(_nseg))
_bayW = _Wd / _npn
_fabW = _bayW * (1 - min(0.95, opening))
# Even panels bunch to the left of their bay, odd panels to the right — which is what a pair does
_bl = eq(_pi % 2, 0)
_pa = _u0 + _pi * _bayW + (1 - _bl) * (_bayW - _fabW)
_du = _fabW / _nseg
_ua = _pa + _si * _du
_ub = _ua + _du
_ph = PI * _si / _sub
_va = _amp * sin(_ph)
_vb = _amp * sin(_ph + PI / _sub)
_nqf = rows(_ua)
Q = hcat(_ua, _va, _ub, _vb, _ub, _vb + _fT, _ua, _va + _fT, fill(_nqf,1,_zBot), fill(_nqf,1,_zTop), fill(_nqf,1,1))
# Quad prism — every part is a quad swept from z0 to z1 (6 faces)
_nq = rows(Q)
_r4 = ones(4,1)
_a1 = col(Q,0)
_b1 = col(Q,1)
_a2 = col(Q,2)
_b2 = col(Q,3)
_a3 = col(Q,4)
_b3 = col(Q,5)
_a4 = col(Q,6)
_b4 = col(Q,7)
_qz0 = col(Q,8)
_qz1 = col(Q,9)
_gq = kron(col(Q,10), _r4)
_fq = kron(arange(_nq), _r4) * 6
_q0 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_qz0,_a2,_b2,_qz0,_a3,_b3,_qz0,_a4,_b4,_qz0), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 0, _gq)
_q1 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_qz1,_a2,_b2,_qz1,_a3,_b3,_qz1,_a4,_b4,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 1, _gq)
_q2 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_qz0,_a2,_b2,_qz0,_a2,_b2,_qz1,_a1,_b1,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 2, _gq)
_q3 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a2,_b2,_qz0,_a3,_b3,_qz0,_a3,_b3,_qz1,_a2,_b2,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 3, _gq)
_q4 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a3,_b3,_qz0,_a4,_b4,_qz0,_a4,_b4,_qz1,_a3,_b3,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 4, _gq)
_q5 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a4,_b4,_qz0,_a1,_b1,_qz0,_a1,_b1,_qz1,_a4,_b4,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 5, _gq)
_FL = vcat(_q0,_q1,_q2,_q3,_q4,_q5)
_PL = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_a2,_b2,_a3,_b3,_a4,_b4), 4*_nq, 2), kron(arange(_nq), _r4), _gq)
# Local (u,v,z) -> world, once, for every part at the same time
_U = _cu + col(_FL,0)
_V = _cv + col(_FL,1)
_W = hcat(_U * _ux + _V * _vx, _U * _uy + _V * _vy, col(_FL,2), col(_FL,3), col(_FL,4))
_nw = rows(_W)
_PU = _cu + col(_PL,0)
_PV = _cv + col(_PL,1)
_WP = hcat(_PU * _ux + _PV * _vx, _PU * _uy + _PV * _vy, col(_PL,2), col(_PL,3))
_nwp = rows(_WP)
Fabric3D = sub(compress(_W, eq(col(_W,4), 1)), 0, 0, _nw, 4)
FabricPlan = sub(compress(_WP, eq(col(_WP,3), 1)), 0, 0, _nwp, 3)
# Rail and finials — axis segments, so a Tube row builds them about their own direction
_RAIL = hcat(_u0 - _ext, 0, _railZ, _u1 + _ext, 0, _railZ, _railR)
_FIN = vcat(hcat(_u0 - _ext - _finR, 0, _railZ, _u0 - _ext, 0, _railZ, _finR), hcat(_u1 + _ext, 0, _railZ, _u1 + _ext + _finR, 0, _railZ, _finR))
_t1u = _cu + col(_RAIL,0)
_t1v = _cv + col(_RAIL,1)
_t2u = _cu + col(_RAIL,3)
_t2v = _cv + col(_RAIL,4)
Rail3D = hcat(_t1u * _ux + _t1v * _vx, _t1u * _uy + _t1v * _vy, col(_RAIL,2), _t2u * _ux + _t2v * _vx, _t2u * _uy + _t2v * _vy, col(_RAIL,5), col(_RAIL,6))
_t1u = _cu + col(_FIN,0)
_t1v = _cv + col(_FIN,1)
_t2u = _cu + col(_FIN,3)
_t2v = _cv + col(_FIN,4)
Finials3D = hcat(_t1u * _ux + _t1v * _vx, _t1u * _uy + _t1v * _vy, col(_FIN,2), _t2u * _ux + _t2v * _vx, _t2u * _uy + _t2v * _vy, col(_FIN,5), col(_FIN,6))
# The rail's PLAN is the same axis segment with z dropped — a Stroke row widens it to the rail diameter
RailPlan = hcat(col(Rail3D,0), col(Rail3D,1), col(Rail3D,3), col(Rail3D,4), 2 * col(Rail3D,6))
# Metrics
openingWidth = _Wd
curtainDrop = _zTop - _zBot
railElevation = _railZ
railLength = _Wd + 2 * _ext
panelCount = _npn
coveredWidth = _npn * _fabW
wavePathLength = sum(len(hcat(_ub - _ua, _vb - _va)))
fullness = _npn * _fabW > 0 ? wavePathLength / (_npn * _fabW) : 0
fabricArea = wavePathLength * (_zTop - _zBot)
